correctness.rationale: For transitive actions, fixed support exhausts the ground set and each invariant block partition is a single orbit; fixed barycentric weights are equal. Block systems correspond bijectively to intervals between point stabilizer and group. For Young actions, classify admissible subset orbits by disjoint translates: complete macroblock unions or full singleton orbits, with precise disjoint-support compatibility. Orbit-simplex fixed barycenters establish a PL model. Duplicating singleton vertices attaches cones along nullhomotopic links, giving a free integral homology splitting; Gottstein's integral basis theorem yields the stated coefficient formula. Both standalone programs were run to completion, including subgroup and Young orbit exhaustions and exact binary boundary calculations. Finite checks supplement but do not establish the universal lemmas.

value.rationale: Two natural infinite group classes yield radically different fixed geometry: transitive actions have discrete fixed spaces detected exactly by imprimitivity/subgroup intervals, while full Young actions have a universal doubled-singleton complex with positive-dimensional torsion-free homology. The subgroup-conjugation module for regular nonabelian actions and all-degree integral Betti formula for infinitely many Young block sizes are mathematically motivated equivariant refinements not encoded by the original nonequivariant homology ranks.
